title: Attack and defend: MAC flooding and VLAN hopping
blurb: See how attackers abuse switch learning and trunk negotiation, then lock down an access port and a trunk.
purpose: MAC flooding and VLAN hopping abuse switch defaults to see or reach traffic that should be separate. In this lab you learn how both attacks work and harden access and trunk ports against them.
scenario: A penetration test report for switch SW3 lists two findings. First, flooding fake MAC addresses made the switch act like a hub. Second, an access port could be turned into a trunk to reach other VLANs. Fix both on user port **GigabitEthernet1/0/20** and trunk **GigabitEthernet1/0/49**.
topology: User port Gi1/0/20 (VLAN 20) ── SW3 ── Gi1/0/49 trunk ── core
objectives: Understand MAC flooding, switch spoofing and double tagging

steps.title: How each attack works
steps.learn: **MAC flooding** fills the switch's CAM table with fake addresses, so it floods frames out every port, where the attacker can capture them. **Switch spoofing** uses DTP to negotiate a trunk from a user port. **Double tagging** sends a frame with two 802.1Q tags: the first matches the trunk's native VLAN and is stripped, and the second carries the frame into the target VLAN.
steps.task: Match each attack to the defense that stops it.

fields.label: MAC flooding
options: Port security with a MAC limit
Turn off DTP (switchport nonegotiate) and hard-code access mode
Use an unused native VLAN and tag it
fields.answer: Port security with a MAC limit

fields.label: Switch spoofing
options: Port security with a MAC limit
Turn off DTP (switchport nonegotiate) and hard-code access mode
Use an unused native VLAN and tag it
fields.answer: Turn off DTP (switchport nonegotiate) and hard-code access mode

fields.label: Double tagging
options: Port security with a MAC limit
Turn off DTP (switchport nonegotiate) and hard-code access mode
Use an unused native VLAN and tag it
fields.answer: Use an unused native VLAN and tag it

steps.title: Harden the access port
steps.task: On **GigabitEthernet1/0/20**: hard-code **access** mode in **VLAN 20**, turn off DTP negotiation, and turn on port security with a **maximum of 1** address and violation mode **shutdown**.
steps.hint: `interface GigabitEthernet1/0/20`, `switchport mode access`, `switchport access vlan 20`, `switchport nonegotiate`, `switchport port-security`, `switchport port-security maximum 1`, `switchport port-security violation shutdown`.

commands.explain: Makes it a fixed access port.

commands.note: The port won't send or answer DTP, so it can't be talked into trunking.
commands.explain: Turns off DTP, so a device can't negotiate a trunk.
Allows a single MAC address, which defeats MAC flooding.
Shuts the port down if another MAC appears.

steps.title: Harden the trunk
steps.learn: Double tagging only works when the attacker's access VLAN equals the trunk's **native VLAN**. Move the native VLAN to an unused one (**999**), allow only the VLANs that are needed, and tag the native VLAN too.
steps.task: On **GigabitEthernet1/0/49**: hard-code **trunk** mode, turn off DTP, set the native VLAN to **999**, and allow only VLANs **10,20,30**. Then tag the native VLAN globally.
steps.hint: `interface GigabitEthernet1/0/49`, `switchport mode trunk`, `switchport nonegotiate`, `switchport trunk native vlan 999`, `switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30`, then `vlan dot1q tag native`.

commands.explain: Enters the trunk to the next switch.
Turns off DTP on the trunk.
Moves the native VLAN to unused VLAN 999, which defeats double tagging.
Allows only the VLANs that need to cross the trunk.

commands.note: Native VLAN frames are tagged too, so a stripped outer tag can't leak into another VLAN.
commands.explain: Tags the native VLAN too, so no traffic crosses untagged.

commands.output:
Name: Gi1/0/20
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Negotiation of Trunking: Off
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (USERS)
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
commands.note: Static access, with trunk negotiation off.
commands.explain: Shows the port's mode and trunking settings.

summary: MAC flooding, switch spoofing and double tagging with their defenses, an access port with static mode, no DTP and port security, and a trunk with no DTP, an unused tagged native VLAN and pruned allowed VLANs.
